thread:
opsbot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/complete (us-east-1) — p95 2.4s (baseline 1.1s), p99 4.1s (baseline 0.9s). Error rate up 3.2x. Customer ticket: C-492 (AcmeCorp).
Emma Li: saw the AcmeCorp ticket — they say timeouts and UX spinner for ~30m. Repro on our side hitting us-east-1 from mimic-agent gives long tails.
Raj Patel: confirming metrics. Rolling window shows spike started ~00:22UTC. We pushed redwood-2.1 config ~00:05UTC but rollout was gradual. Not sure if related yet.
Theo Ramirez: quick thought: prioritize mitigations -> 1) circuit-break model routing for heavy customers, 2) fallback to redwood-compact-v1 for latency-sensitive routes, 3) enforce per-tenant RPS limits for AcmeCorp while we stabilize.
Sara Kim: repro curl from mimic-agent:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/complete \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' --max-time 12
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout\nConnection: close
```
Tools: tail of proxy logs shows many connections with long backend RTTs and occasional 5xx.
Louise Chen: kicking off mitigations now: 1) enabling circuit breaker on edge for /v1/complete (drop >200ms backend RTT to fallback), 2) apply temporary tenant throttle for AcmeCorp -> 30rps, 3) trigger model fallback for low-latency route to redwood-compact-v1. Executing commands.
Louise Chen: (cmd) kubectl -n prod scale deployment inference-proxy --replicas=10 — scaling frontend.
Raj Patel: also increasing dedicated pool capacity: infra API call -> POST /infra/scale {"pool":"dedicated-us-east-1","delta":4}. Rolling now.
Theo Ramirez: if rollback of the redwood-2.1 rollout is needed, flip the feature flag: curl -X POST https://internal-console/flags -d '{"model:redwood-2.1":"disabled"}' (ops only).
opsbot: ACTION: circuit-breaker enabled for /v1/complete, fallback route to redwood-compact-v1 active for latency-priority. Tenant throttle for AcmeCorp set to 30rps. Autoscale request accepted.
Raj Patel: watching metrics — p99 starting to trend down: 4.1s -> 2.0s in last 2 minutes. Error rate dropping.
Emma Li: reached out to AcmeCorp support contact, told them we're applying mitigations and will update in 10m. They reported partial improvement in the UI. :thumbsup:
Sara Kim: quick note — KV prefix cache miss rate was high for this workload. Enabling prefix caching for common prompts might help reduce backend pressure.
Louise Chen: added an immediate cache config: POST /config/cache {"prefix_cache":true, "paths":["/v1/complete"]}.
opsbot: MONITOR: p95=1.3s, p99=1.7s (us-east-1) after mitigations. No new 5xx for 5m.
Raj Patel: leaving one person on watch (me) for 2h and will follow up with postmortem if rollback or root cause required. Assigning incident owner: Raj.
Emma Li: thanks team — closing customer loop: told AcmeCorp we'll continue to monitor and open a long-term ticket for quantization/throughput optimizations.
Louise Chen: follow-ups: 1) correlate rollout segments for redwood-2.1 -> strong suspect, 2) investigate KV cache hit regression, 3) SRE to propose stricter SLO guardrail (auto-fallback + tenant throttles) so this is automatic next time.
Theo Ramirez: noted — will draft mitigation playbook adding explicit quick-check list and exact CLI/API commands.
opsbot: Incident logged: INC-2026-349. Keep thread updates here.
